newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's SEC okays proxy exemptions of four firms.
newsitem.headline: Manila's SEC okays proxy exemptions of four firms.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved on Thursday the exemption of four publicly-listed companies from the new proxy rule for their 1997 stockholders meetings.

Documents from the SEC showed requests for exemptions by the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Philippine Tobacco Flue Curing Redrying Corp, Philex Mining Corp and Bogo-Medellin Milling Co Inc were granted.
The SEC has imposed stricter rules on proxy votes gathering and voting including uniform proxy statements and forms.

The four companies said they may not be able to comply with the requirements in the filing of proxy materials with the SEC and their distribution to shareholders as their annual stockholder meetings are scheduled in the first quarter of this year.
The new proxy rules, the companies said, will require the amendment of company by-laws to adjust schedules for nominations to the board.
The SEC approved the requests provided necessary changes in the by-laws are presented to and approved by stockholders in their annual meeting this year.
